title: Misr El Amria workers’ strike over minimum-wage application and pay conditions
location: Misr El Amria Spinning & Weaving Company, Alexandria
participants_original: CFJ reports approximately 1,000 workers were on strike by Aug 20; this count is not a documented count of a simultaneous public gathering.
threshold_50_evidence: A work stoppage at the company is reported, but neither source establishes that workers gathered publicly outside the workplace or made a direct government demand; project eligibility remains open.

start_date.summary: Al Manassa dates the strike to July 30; CFJ’s Aug20 account independently identifies the same July 30 onset.

end_date.summary: Neither body reports a verified end date; CFJ says the action was ongoing on Aug20.

location.summary: Both reports place the strike at Misr El Amria Spinning and Weaving in Alexandria.

scope.summary: One company site in Alexandria is reported.

organizer.summary: Workers are identified, but no organizer or union is named.

demands.summary: Workers objected to the application of the statutory minimum wage and pay arrangements, and sought salary/arrears changes and dismissal of company executives.

participants_original.summary: CFJ describes the striking workers as numbering about 1,000; it does not identify whether this is a simultaneous public crowd count.

participants_min.summary: No minimum for a simultaneous public gathering is established.

participants_max.summary: Approximate strike-group size is not a verified maximum of a public gathering.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A roughly 1,000-person strike is reported, but public gathering/simultaneous turnout is not established.

state_target.summary: Worker demands reported in the bodies primarily address company management; minimum-wage policy is implicated, but a direct demand to the Egyptian State or public action is not documented.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed bodies do not report violence by workers; unknown.

state_response.summary: CFJ reports summons and pressure from National Security, while Al Manassa reports a wage offer by an officer. Neither is coded as arrests or an implemented accommodation from these accounts.

eligibility.summary: The episode is a workplace strike; public forum/direct government targeting is unresolved under the codebook.

open_questions: Did workers take the action into a public forum or directly press government authorities to enforce state labor policy, as required by the codebook?
Does the approximately 1,000-worker strike count represent simultaneous participation at a specific action, rather than the workforce or cumulative work stoppage?
notes: Ccode 651 is provisional from planning/countries_provisional.csv; official baseline assignment is pending.
